newsitem.title: USA: Duff & Phelps raises Ralston notes rating.
newsitem.headline: Duff & Phelps raises Ralston notes rating.

text.p: Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co said Friday it raised its rating on Ralston Purina Co notes and debentures to single-A-minus from triple-B-plus.
The rating change involves about $2.4 billion of the company's debt, Duff & Phelps said.
The credit rating agency also said it rated Ralston's proposed offering of $360 million mandatory exchangeable notes due 2000 at single-A-minus.

Ralston has completed several strategic moves to improve and refocus on its core businesses during the last three years, Duff & Phelps said. Ralston has divested lower-margined, cyclical and noncore operations and intends to divest its international agricultural business during the first quarter of 1998.

"We view these steps as significantly positive," the rating agency said. "Furthermore Ralston continues to evaluate and restructure its battery business to increase its competitiveness and profitability."

"Ralston's profitability and operting cash flow are strong and stable," it said. "The company's credit protection measures are likely to improve in the intermediate term, reflecting increased operating earnings and lower debt levels."
